title: Term length bounded by DNF width
statement: Let $f$ be a DNF formula in $n$ variables, that is, a disjunction $t_1 \vee \cdots \vee t_m$ of terms, where each term is a conjunction of literals, and let its width be the largest number of literals occurring in any of its terms (and $0$ if $f$ has no terms). Then for every term $t$ appearing in $f$, the number of literals in $t$ is at most the width of $f$.
hypotheses_covered: t is a term appearing in the DNF formula f
replaced: Every term $t$ belonging to a DNF $f$ has length at most the width of $f$.
